grh_ae8a987c726c9980ddc1.title: As You Wish
paragraphs: Chicago factory worker Eddie Meagan buys an old lamp at a yard sale and discovers a genie who grants him five wishes. Eddie quickly learns that careless wording has consequences: offhand remarks count as wishes, and wishing never to work again leaves him fired rather than rich. His wife sells the lamp to raise money for their son Larry's birthday present, forcing Eddie through a frantic search to recover it while police and other complications gather around him. After using a wish to make everyone forget the trouble surrounding the lamp, Eddie spends his last real wish on the finest piano in the world for Larry. His family is delighted, and soon afterward a friend unexpectedly brings word that Eddie has been offered a better factory job. Eddie ends up happier through family and ordinary good fortune than through the selfish wishes he first imagined.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on April 3, 1979. It is listed as episode 42 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Norman Alden, Jean Gillespie, Marvin Miller, Lou Horne, and Jack Carol. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Mark Trella as writer, and Andy Griffith as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_aeaf8f1cc78285df1586.title: The Silver Buckle
paragraphs: Two train robbers kill passenger Carl Davis after mistaking the silver-colored buckle on his anniversary belt for real silver. Later Britt meets brothers Kit and Lex Springer, who claim to be posse members hunting the bandits for a reward and ask him to guide them through Miller Pass. A bloodstain on Kit's fancy belt and other inconsistencies make Britt suspicious, and he overhears the brothers admit they are the robbers before they try to kill him. Britt survives the ambush long enough for the real posse to arrive; during Kit's attempted escape, his horse goes over the trail edge and the stolen belt catches on the saddle, leaving him fatally trapped by the very buckle that marked the crime.
